subject: Gradual activation timetable and integration safeguards for Aperture Financial
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@aperturefin.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aperturefin.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: detailed activation timeline & safeguards for RFP response

Jonas —

Thanks for the initial RFP materials. Our procurement and engineering teams reviewed the high-level approach and have a few gaps around how the activation will be sequenced and what rollback / stop-the-line checks you'll have during the first 30 days. For compliance we'll need: a day-by-day activation timetable for the pilot and first four weeks of production, the integration test matrix (auth, telemetry, data flows), and explicit fallback triggers (thresholds for latency/error/%failed requests) plus contact/escalation steps.

Can you send a consolidated response we can include in the procurement packet by Apr 28? We also need to understand if any onboarding work requires our side to expose data-plane endpoints or IP allowlists.

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a short call if helpful.

— Sarah Liu
VP IT Operations, Aperture Financial

From: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@aperturefin.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, CloudBridge Integration <cloudbridge@partner.co>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: detailed activation timeline & safeguards for RFP response

Sarah —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached is a first-pass deliverable: "redwood-activation-timetable-v1.pdf" plus an "integration-checklist-aperture.xlsx" that maps tests to owners. Main highlights:

- Pilot window (Week 0–2): sandbox connectivity, telemetry validation, low-volume traffic (1–5% of production). No customer PII flows until Week 2 sign-off.
- Gradual activation (Week 2–6): increment traffic in three gates (10%, 40%, 100%) with 24–48 hour evaluation windows.
- Acceptance gates: latency p95 < 120ms, error rate < 0.5% sustained over 1 hour, and no regressions on the provided prompt-eval set.
- Fallbacks: automatic traffic diversion to a warm-compatible model variant and region failover. Manual stop-the-line if any gate fails twice.

Operational asks from Aperture: IP allowlist for dedicated VPC egress (we can provide CIDR blocks), and SAML metadata to configure SP-initiated SSO for the admin console. We call out these items in the checklist with owners and expected lead times.

Can Priyom and Kim confirm the SLA/rollback wording and whether CloudBridge should be included as an active participant for the sandbox connectivity tasks?

I can consolidate a procurement-ready narrative by Apr 27 once we incorporate the internal edits. If a short call helps, I'm free Thu morning.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-activation-timetable-v1.pdf (17KB, summary), integration-checklist-aperture.xlsx (12KB)

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 13:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: detailed activation timeline & safeguards for RFP response

Looping in details on the rollout controls. Quick notes inline: 

- Gate metrics: change p95 threshold to 150ms for initial region (we should call out an uplift window) and document a staged optimization plan.
- Error surface: specify how we measure "failed requests" (distinct 4xx/5xx vs application-level quality failures). Recommend: 5xx + >=2 LLM hallucination-regression flags from the eval harness within a 1h window triggers manual halt.
- Rollback: automated traffic diversion should include a TTL to avoid oscillation (30 min drain), and we need an ops runbook reference.

I've added comments to the spreadsheet and drafted a short ops-runbook stub (see integration-checklist -> tab "OpsSteps"). Kim — can you verify that the warm model variant we plan to use is covered in the licensing section of the MOU?

If all looks good I'll merge and hand the procurement narrative to Jonas for final copy.

— Priyom
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@aperturefin.com>
Cc: CloudBridge Integration <cloudbridge@partner.co>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: detailed activation timeline & safeguards for RFP response

Sarah / team —

Thanks for the review items. A few clarifications that will appear in the procurement-ready doc: 

1) Licensing / warm model: Aperture's MOU will include rights for the warm-compatible variant used during diversion. We'll call out CPU/GPU quantization options and the fallback model's throughput characteristics.

2) Network & onboarding: Redwood needs one static egress block for the dedicated VPC peering — we can give those CIDRs plus a short maintenance blackout calendar for initial deployment. CloudBridge — please confirm which subnet the integration agent will live in so we can include exact routes.

3) Telemetry & thresholds: Priyom's suggested escalation (>=2 eval-harness regressions within 1h) is acceptable. We'll also include a smoke-test checklist executed after each gate (auth smoke, sample inference checks, trace sampling).

Jonas — happy to accept the final narrative. I've attached a draft MOU (MOU-Aperture-Redwood-draft.docx) with the narrow licensing language for the fallback model.

— Kim Park
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Attachments: MOU-Aperture-Redwood-draft.docx (24KB)

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@aperturefin.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@aperturefin.com, CloudBridge Integration <cloudbridge@partner.co>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: detailed activation timeline & safeguards for RFP response

Team —

This is great, thank you. The procurement team reviewed the timetable and MOU draft; only a couple of minor edits and we should be ready to proceed to signature. Two quick items: 1) can you add a short clause about data residency for logging/telemetry (we require logs to remain in our US tenancy until 90 days retention) and 2) please confirm the SAML attributes Aperture needs for console access (we expect email, firstName, lastName, role).

I've attached the procurement checklist as PDF for our internal use; we've also prepared a DocuSign envelope — link below — to push the MOU forward after the small updates. Proposed kickoff (post-signature): Mon May 10, 2027 — pilot sandbox access, 1-week sandbox validation then gradual activation per your timetable.

DocuSign envelope: https://app.docusign.com/envelopes/ENV-APF-2027-087

I'll wait for the updated MOU and the small telemetry/data-residency paragraph before we sign.

Thanks again — look forward to kicking this off.

— Sarah
VP IT Operations, Aperture Financial

Attachments: procurement-checklist-aperture.pdf (7KB)
